CF-agg.detail: keccak256 (Ethereum Keccak-256 of holon/keccak.py, over the domain value's 32-byte words) gives 273 pairwise different images on the fixed sample of List<Nat> (a test on a sample, not a proof)

instance.reason: each law states its own finite set S; CF(p, S) is inhabited per law by the instance (holon.inhabit, non_vacuity.witness)

CF-hdr.reason: No fact document the M2 models are compiled from calls hdr_hash: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json compares a presented parent header with the stored batch by index and field equality (parent == lci and the stored csr == prev, Rollup.sol:312-314), never by hashing the header's bytes, so no M2 model transition consults this parameter. Routing it needs a facts document whose commit actions hash the presented header (the extracted facts, BUILD_PLAN I17-I20), not an edit of the M1 facts (audit M2/1 F-M2-11). Until then the stand-in stays inside the model (ledger CF-keccak-headers).

Hyp-ISubmitter.reason: ISubmitter is stateful: isActive changes with staking and with the slashing the rollup itself triggers (_challengerWin), so it is not a function of its arguments that a model could take as a parameter. M2 keeps the M1 stand-in inside the model (active-list membership, challengeDeposit = DEP, a slash removes the submitter from the active list; ledger oracle-ISubmitter) until the staking contract is extracted (BUILD_PLAN I36).

Hyp-messenger.reason: The messenger's modelled behaviour is a state update of the rollup's own message queue (sendMessage appends one message): part of the transition, not a value the model queries. M2 keeps the M1 stand-in inside the model (ledger oracle-messenger) until the messenger and the queue are extracted (BUILD_PLAN I36).

HypC.reason: The circuits are not modelled: the verifier entry's proof == 1 rule stands in for them. The public input and HypC are extracted in BUILD_PLAN I37.

HypF.reason: The node's L1 fetcher lies outside the M2 bundle: the models take batch data as action inputs.

HypP.reason: No M2 model reaches L2 state: the predeploys lie outside the M2 bundle (the L1 rollup contract and the batch data).

HypSeal.reason: The sequencer's sealing loop is not modelled: batches enter the models as action inputs.

HypT.reason: Transactions are opaque tokens in every M2 model. The Go transaction codec is extracted with the Go frontend (BUILD_PLAN I18).

HypV-proof1.reason: No fact document the M2 models are compiled from calls verify: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json states the verifier as the inline guards ['==', 'proof', 1] (commitBatchWithProof, reason 22) and ['||', 'timeout', ['==', 'proof', 1]] (proveState, reason 22), src 'oracle: IRollupVerifier.verifyAggregateProof', so no M2 model transition consults this parameter and the proof == 1 rule is a stand-in inside the model. Routing it needs a facts document whose actions call verify(proof) (the extracted facts, BUILD_PLAN I17-I20), not an edit of the M1 facts (audit M2/1 F-M2-11). Until then the stand-in stays inside the model (ledger oracle-verifier); the hypothesis and its instance are kept as the record of that rule.

HypZ.reason: No M2 model calls the compression codec: batch data are opaque tokens. The Go codec is modelled at loop granularity, with HypZ as its hypothesis, in BUILD_PLAN I38.
